receipt.public_excerpt: “We’re going to end up with complete autonomy, and I think we will have complete autonomy in approximately two years.”

evidence_items.explanation: The original interview establishes the attributed prediction. Musk separately allowed additional time for regulatory approval, so the prediction concerned technical capability first.

evidence_items.locator: Opening account of Autonomy Day; subsequent dated chronology

receipt.public_excerpt: I feel very confident predicting autonomous robo taxis for Tesla by next year.

evidence_items.explanation: Reports the 2019 robotaxi forecast. Its chronology also documents a 2016 coast-to-coast forecast, a 2017 two-year sleeping-at-the-wheel forecast, and a 2018 forecast of full self-driving the following year.

receipt.public_excerpt: Tesla will be able to make its vehicles completely autonomous by the end of this year, founder Elon Musk has said.

evidence_items.explanation: Documents another near-term prediction in 2020, explicitly concerning autonomy without driver input.

receipt.public_excerpt: “I’m confident based on my understanding of the technical roadmap and the progress that we’re making between each beta iteration,” Musk said.

evidence_items.explanation: The preceding paragraph identifies this as Musk's answer about achieving Level 5 by the end of 2021. This extends the recurring short-timeline pattern into 2021.

evidence_items.locator: Introduction describing January and February ride-alongs

receipt.public_excerpt: All three drivers understood that the technology does not make their Tesla electric cars fully self driving, despite the brand name.

evidence_items.explanation: Direct ride-alongs documented continuing supervision and interventions. The article also reports Musk's renewed prediction, on the 2021 year-end earnings call, of achieving full self-driving during 2022.

receipt.public_excerpt: Beginning today, October 8, we’re excited to open up our fully driverless offering to Waymo One riders.

evidence_items.explanation: Driverless service existed at another company within a limited service area. This is material to the wording's scope, but does not establish that Tesla fulfilled Musk's predictions.
